source: NCERT Class XII, Introductory Macroeconomics, Ch. 4 (Determination of Income and Employment).

sections.heading: 1. Aggregate Demand and Supply
points: **Aggregate Demand (AD)** = total planned expenditure in the economy = **C (consumption) + I (investment) + G (government spending) + (X − M) (net exports)**.
**Aggregate Supply (AS)** = total value of goods/services produced (= national income).
**Equilibrium income** is where **AD = AS** (planned spending = output).

sections.heading: 2. Consumption and Saving
points: **Consumption function:** C = a + bY (a = autonomous consumption; b = **Marginal Propensity to Consume, MPC**).
**MPC** = change in consumption ÷ change in income; **MPS (Marginal Propensity to Save)** = 1 − MPC.
**Saving = Income − Consumption**; at equilibrium, planned saving = planned investment (S = I).

sections.heading: 3. The Investment Multiplier
points: The **multiplier (k)** shows how a change in investment leads to a **larger change in income**.
**Multiplier k = 1 ÷ (1 − MPC) = 1 ÷ MPS**.
A higher MPC → a larger multiplier; an initial injection (investment/spending) multiplies through successive rounds of spending.

sections.heading: 4. Full Employment, and Gaps
points: **Full employment** = when all willing workers at the going wage are employed; involves only **frictional/voluntary** unemployment.
**Deflationary (recessionary) gap** — AD is less than needed for full employment (output/employment below potential).
**Inflationary gap** — AD exceeds full-employment output (causes inflation).
**Keynes** argued that government spending can fill a deflationary gap and raise employment.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: AD = C + I + G + (X − M); equilibrium: AD = AS (and S = I).
MPC = ΔC/ΔY; MPS = 1 − MPC.
Multiplier k = 1 ÷ (1 − MPC) = 1 ÷ MPS.
Deflationary gap = AD too low; Inflationary gap = AD too high.
Keynes: government spending fills the deflationary gap.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Multiplier = 1 ÷ (1 − MPC) = 1 ÷ MPS**.
**MPS = 1 − MPC** (they sum to 1).
**Deflationary gap = deficient demand; inflationary gap = excess demand.**
At equilibrium, **planned saving = planned investment (S = I)**.
